title: Veo's duration slider is a lie that misprices the run - lock it to the 8 seconds Veo returns
description: Follow-up to MPI-879, which bounded the duration slider by each cloud model's published range. Veo 3.1 publishes NO duration field at all (dev_configs/deepinfra-prices.json, google/veo-3.1 and google/veo-3.1-fast carry aspect_ratio, resolution and sample_count, nothing else), so buildSizeFields emits no duration and the clip comes back a fixed length whatever the slider says. MPI-879 deliberately left it on the app's 1-30. Fabio, 2026-09-21: lock it to min 8, max 8. THE MONEY, measured 2026-09-21: Veo is priced per output second (cents_per_output_sec 40) and deepinfraPricing.js:161 and :178 read "opts.duration || CLIP_SECONDS[modelId]" - the control's number WINS over the fixed 8. At the shipped default of 3 s the price tag quotes USD 1.20 for veo-31-cloud while the run bills USD 3.20; dragged to 30 it quotes USD 12.00 for that same USD 3.20 clip. veo-31-fast-cloud: USD 0.45 quoted against USD 1.20, and USD 4.50 at 30. Under-quoting at the DEFAULT is the live case - nobody has to touch the slider to be told the wrong price. THE COMPONENT TRAP: MpiProgressBar does take min and max as props (MPI-879 drives both), but its fill maths is ((value - min) / (max - min)) * 100 at MpiProgressBar.js:49 and :88 - min === max is 0/0, so a locked 8-8 slider paints width: NaN% and handle left: NaN%. Either guard that (fall back to 100% when max <= min) or do not mount a slider at all for a fixed-length model and render a static '8 s' line instead. SINGLE SOURCE: the 8 already exists as CLIP_SECONDS in deepinfraPricing.js:107, which is not exported. Export it, or add a fixedDurationFor(endpointId) beside durationRangeFor - do NOT retype the literal in PromptBoxControls.js. Also decide whether Input_Duration should be injected at all for Veo: our pricing reads it, the provider never does.
